title: Calling for help
summary: Who to call and what to say so that help arrives quickly.
steps: Protect yourself and the victim from further accidents.

Call 112 (emergency number in Europe, also redirected in many other countries) or 911 in North America; in France also 15 (medical), 18 (fire), 17 (police), 114 by text for deaf or hard-of-hearing people.
Give: the exact location, what happened, the number of victims, their condition (breathing? conscious?).
Never hang up first: wait for instructions.
tips: 112 goes through any available mobile network, even another operator's.
If the network is saturated, a text message often gets through better than a call.

title: Cardiac arrest: CPR
summary: A person is unresponsive and not breathing normally: every minute counts.
steps: Check: the person does not react when you talk to them and shake their shoulders, and is not breathing normally.
Have someone call 112 / 911 and ask for a defibrillator (AED).
Lay the person on their back on a hard surface.
Hands one on top of the other in the centre of the chest, arms straight.
Push hard: press down 5 to 6 cm, at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute.
If you are trained: 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths. Otherwise, continuous chest compressions only.
As soon as the defibrillator arrives, switch it on and follow its voice instructions.
Keep going without stopping until rescuers take over or normal breathing returns.
warnings: Don't be afraid of doing it wrong: without CPR, the chances of survival drop very quickly.
tips: Rhythm: the beat of the song “Stayin' Alive” is about 100 compressions per minute.

title: Stop severe bleeding
summary: Blood is flowing heavily: apply pressure immediately.
steps: Lay the victim down.
Press hard directly on the wound, with a protected hand (glove, plastic bag) or a clean cloth.
Keep the pressure on without letting go; add cloth on top if blood soaks through, without removing the first one.
Replace your hand with a tight pressure bandage if possible.
On a limb, if pressure is not enough: tourniquet 5 to 7 cm above the wound, tightened until the bleeding stops; note the time it was applied.
warnings: Never loosen or remove a tourniquet once applied: that is the rescuers' job.
Do not remove an object stuck in the wound: apply pressure around it.

title: Choking (adult)
summary: The person can no longer speak, cough or breathe.
steps: If they are coughing effectively: encourage them to cough, do nothing else.
If they can no longer cough or speak: lean them forward and give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
If that fails: up to 5 abdominal thrusts (stand behind, fist above the navel, pull hard towards you and upwards).
Alternate 5 blows and 5 thrusts until the object comes out.
If they lose consciousness: call 112 / 911 and start CPR.
warnings: For pregnant or obese people, thrusts are given on the chest, not the abdomen.
The technique is different for infants: get specific training.

title: Recovery position
summary: An unconscious person who is breathing: put them on their side to protect their airway.
steps: Check that they are breathing normally.
Place the arm nearest to you at a right angle, palm up.
Bring the other hand against their cheek, on your side, and hold it there.
Raise the far leg, knee bent, foot on the ground.
Pull on the knee to roll the person towards you.
Adjust the leg to stabilise them, open the mouth, check breathing regularly.
warnings: If breathing stops: roll them onto their back and start CPR.

title: Burns
summary: Cool immediately, for a long time, with lukewarm water.
steps: Cool under lukewarm running water (15 to 25 °C) for at least 10 minutes, ideally 20.
Remove rings, watches and clothing around the burn if they are not stuck.
Cover with cling film or a clean, lint-free cloth.
Call for help if the burn is larger than half the victim's palm, affects the face, hands or genitals, or if the victim is a child.
warnings: No ice, butter, toothpaste or oil.
Do not burst blisters.
Save water: in a shortage, non-drinkable but clear water can be used for cooling.

title: Hypothermia
summary: The body is getting dangerously cold: shivering, confusion, clumsiness.
steps: Get the person out of the wind and insulate them from the ground (cardboard, branches, bag).
Replace wet clothes with dry ones.
Cover the whole body, head included (space blanket, sleeping bag).
If they are conscious and swallowing well: hot, sweet drinks.
Handle them gently and call for help if they are confused or have stopped shivering.
warnings: No alcohol.
Do not rub the limbs.
A person who stops shivering while still cold is in serious danger.

title: Recognising a stroke
summary: Face, arms, speech: at the slightest sign, call immediately.
steps: Face: ask them to smile; is the mouth drooping on one side?
Arms: ask them to raise both arms; does one drift down?
Speech: ask them to repeat a simple sentence; are the words confused or slurred?
At the slightest of these signs: call 112 / 911 immediately.
Note the time the symptoms started: it determines which treatment is possible.
Lay the person down or make them comfortable, give them nothing to eat or drink.
warnings: Even if the signs go away, call anyway: it is often the warning of a severe stroke.

title: Severe allergic reaction
summary: Swelling of the face, difficulty breathing after a sting, a food or a medicine.
steps: If the person has an adrenaline auto-injector: help them use it on the outer thigh (through clothing if needed).
Sit them up if they are struggling to breathe, lay them down with legs raised if they are pale or weak.
If there is no improvement after 5 minutes and a second injector is available: give a second injection.
Monitor breathing; if it stops, start CPR.
warnings: Do not make the person walk or stand up suddenly.

title: Asthma attack
steps: Sit the person up, leaning slightly forward, and reassure them.
Help them take their reliever treatment (bronchodilator inhaler, often blue) as prescribed.
Loosen clothing, move them away from smoke, dust or cold.
Call 112 / 911 if the attack does not ease, if they can no longer speak or if their lips turn blue.

title: Fracture, sprain, dislocation
summary: Do not move the limb, immobilise it as it is.
steps: Do not try to put the limb back in place or straighten it.
Immobilise it in the position found: wedge it with rolled-up clothes, or tie it to a splint (stick, cardboard, rolled magazine) covering the joint above and below.
For an arm: a sling made from a scarf or a T-shirt.
Open fracture (bone visible): cover with a clean cloth without pressing on the bone, stop the bleeding around it.
Apply cold wrapped in cloth for sprains and pain, 20 minutes maximum.
Have someone call for help or get to a health professional.
warnings: Suspected back or neck injury (fall from height, accident): do not move the victim unless in immediate danger, ask them not to move their head.

title: Heatstroke
summary: Burning skin, headache, confusion: cool them without waiting.
steps: Move the person into the shade or somewhere cool, lay them down.
Call 112 / 911 if they are confused, vomiting or lose consciousness.
Remove unnecessary clothing, spray them with cool water and fan them continuously.
Place wet cloths on the neck, armpits and groin.
If they are fully conscious: give them cool water in small sips.
warnings: Give nothing to drink to an unconscious or confused person: recovery position if they are breathing.

title: Bites and stings
summary: Dog, snake, tick, wasp: the right actions.
steps: Animal bite: wash thoroughly with soap and water for 5 minutes, disinfect, and see a doctor (risk of infection and rabies).
Snake bite: stay calm and still, lay the victim down, remove rings and bracelets, immobilise the limb, call 112 / 911.
Tick: remove it as soon as possible with a tick remover by twisting, without crushing it, then disinfect; watch for a red patch spreading in the following weeks and see a doctor if it appears.
Wasp or bee: remove the sting by scraping it with a fingernail or a card, apply cold. Call 112 / 911 for a sting in the mouth or a whole-body reaction.
warnings: Snake: no tourniquet, no cutting, no sucking out the venom.
Tick: do not use ether, alcohol or any product before removing it.

title: Choking infant (under one year)
summary: The baby can no longer cry, cough or breathe.
steps: Lay the baby face down along your forearm, head lower than the body, supporting the jaw.
Give up to 5 back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
If the object has not come out: turn them face up onto the other forearm, head lower.
Give up to 5 chest thrusts with two fingers in the centre of the chest, just below the nipple line.
Alternate 5 blows and 5 thrusts; have someone call 112 / 911.
If the baby loses consciousness: start infant resuscitation.
warnings: Never hang the baby upside down by the feet or sweep blindly for the object with a finger.
Hands-on training in paediatric first aid is strongly recommended.
